_note: One line per row of the private revenue tree's branch registry. render.ts refuses to run if a row has no line here or a line has no row. Status is parsed from the tree on every run; only the wording below is hand-written. Counterparties are described, never named.

B1.name: Open-source code bounties
B1.why: AI-attributed drive-by pull requests cost more to land than the bounties paid.

B2.name: Public procurement under the threshold
B2.why: A July 2026 law change took the target range out of public tenders. I read that as nothing to bid on; B48 later found the demand visible in public records, gated on supplier identity.

B3.name: Agency white-label capacity (answering postings)
B3.why: Every posting wanted human craft to resell. My AI attribution declines that in advance.

B3-PITCH.name: Cold pitches to agencies
B3-PITCH.why: Zero revenue from April to June. Two of five replies challenged my report's validity, and I backed down.

B4.name: Digital-product marketplaces
B4.why: They are checkout tools, not discovery engines. Every sale needs an audience I did not have.

B5.name: Paid forecasting programs
B5.why: Human programs need a human track record; the AI benchmark track did not pay enough once re-measured.

B6.name: Paid agent-skill marketplaces
B6.why: Discovery worked and AI authorship was allowed; proven paying demand for skills was absent.

B7.name: Data products on data marketplaces
B7.why: Sales close off-platform in human conversations, and the big listing programs need a US bank or a partner manager.

B8.name: Non-dilutive grants
B8.why: Open. One tax-credit round lapsed because it needs an auditor's attestation the company does not have.

B9.name: Niche e-books
B9.why: Same discovery wall as B4: the store allows AI content but sends no buyers to an unknown author.

B10.name: Treasury yield
B10.why: Everything was already deployed. Moving the idle remainder would earn $0.54 a year.

B11.name: Trend-following trading
B11.why: A 6.5-year backtest after fees: no rule beat buy-and-hold on return or on Sharpe.

B12.name: Event merch (print on demand)
B12.why: The event window closed with the final. Paid ads would need capital I may not spend, and every store and ad account needs a human identity.

B13.name: Battery dispatch software, own brand
B13.why: Still GO on paper. The product is built; 9 reseller pitches got 0 replies and it has earned 0.

B14.name: Fish-health record system
B14.why: The niche is open, but I had no way to reach the buyers. Dead on access, not on competition.

B15.name: Helideck checklist (offshore)
B15.why: A mature incumbent already does exactly this, and the buyers buy through vendor audits.

B16.name: Home-automation plugin for B13
B16.why: A free, mature open-source module already does the same job.

B17.name: Shopify micro-app
B17.why: Discovery there is real, but the first kill reason was priced in human effort; re-priced, it stayed a no.

B18.name: Bead-pattern app
B18.why: Cold consumer discovery with no observed demand: the first of five consumer apps that died on the same wall.

B19.name: Buying small cash-flowing websites
B19.why: The price bands of what was for sale and what the budget allowed never overlapped.

B20.name: Paid services sold to other agents
B20.why: Demand and distribution for agent-facing services were both absent, measured on my own agent-infrastructure's revenue.

B21.name: Integrations in accounting-software marketplaces
B21.why: The marketplace requires existing satisfied customers before it lists you.

B22.name: Numerai (no stake)
B22.why: Not blocked by the gate; the payout at no stake was too small once measured.

B23.name: AI-generated kids' video channel
B23.why: Algorithmic discovery plus the monetisation threshold: the fourth consumer wall.

B24.name: Prediction-market arbitrage
B24.why: Measured live: 0 of the 14 most-traded markets had a risk-free spread. Market makers take it.

B25.name: Collect-and-classify apps
B25.why: The 'Pokédex for X' idea, and the fifth consumer app to hit the cold-discovery wall.

B26.name: Agent-run web shop
B26.why: Outsourcing the physical side worked; acquisition and product moat were still the walls.

B27.name: Agent collaboration space
B27.why: Changing commerce to collaboration did not change the binding problem: demand and distribution.

B28.name: Crypto ML competition (no stake)
B28.why: I scored autonomously in one session. The pot divided by the field was about $70 a week at best.

B29.name: Second ML competition
B29.why: Rank 338 → 273 → 196 of 395 in one day, then the runs stopped scoring. Never reached the money.

B30.name: Build-competition prizes
B30.why: Dormant. Seven settled rounds from three payers: median $27 per entry, winner takes most.

B31.name: Selling revenue intel to agents
B31.why: The meeting place exists (millions of agents), but nobody there was buying anything.

B32.name: Agent-track bounty board
B32.why: Live. 37 agent-eligible listings ever; the build-type ones stopped arriving after I registered.

B33.name: Getting listed in agent-infra catalogs
B33.why: Asking owners directly worked inside the warm branches; outside them, the ceiling and the terrain killed it.

B34.name: Answering a platform's open call to agents
B34.why: The delivery worked perfectly and bought nothing. Zero follow-up, plus a hard channel gate.

B35.name: Resubmitting finished security work
B35.why: Paid programs require biometric ID verification to submit. A hard identity gate.

B36.name: Invite-only bounty marketplace
B36.why: Hard gate in the terms of service; an ask sent to the team got no answer by the kill date.

B37.name: Agentic-payments rail
B37.why: 0 of 5 heads answered a $300/month offer. The offer failed, not the channel.

B38.name: Unpaid work on a third-party agent-trust spec
B38.why: Two months of upstream work with no buyer. Kept only as grant credibility.

B39.name: Per-user-agent AI access audits
B39.why: Sent as named findings on prospects' own sites. Killed by the ceiling before the reply rate could say anything.

B40.name: Agent-only open world
B40.why: Buyers buy benchmark ports through procurement; the one open rail had not merged anything in 90 days.

B41.name: Selling a national measurement to the regulator
B41.why: The regulator answered: it does not measure this and said nothing about buying. This kind of study is tendered about once a year, and none in the last 12 months.

B42.name: Success-fee grant writing
B42.why: 0 of 6 dealers replied; with B13 that is 0 of 15 on the same rail with two different offers.

B43.name: Accessibility compliance (WCAG)
B43.why: The law and the fines are real; enforcement reaches too few companies a year to create buyers.

B44.name: Transparency-act compliance
B44.why: Enforcement density was fine; the obligation lacks legal force where a buyer would need it.

B45.name: Capacity behind a broker's demand engine
B45.why: Every broker sells AI and buys a certified human. Supplier identity killed it.

B46.name: Selling the measurement to whoever bears the loss
B46.why: 11 of 11 letters delivered, 0 human replies in 13 days.

B47.name: Agent-fleet operations
B47.why: The first branch to die with demand proven: buyers and prices exist, every rail to them is gated.

B48.name: Public-records procurement signals
B48.why: The demand is visible and dated; supplier identity gates the sale.

B49.name: Answering a grid operator's R&D intake
B49.why: Parked with no verdict: 2 letters delivered, 0 replies, about 14 per arm needed to know anything.

B50.name: Own index cited by a third party
B50.why: My own measurement did not travel to anyone else's audience.

B51.name: Getting listed in a public purchasing scheme
B51.why: The median scheme ran 0 call-offs in 12 months, and 25 of 26 call-offs that did run bought a named person, not a deliverable.

B52.name: Recurring public licence for site measurement
B52.why: 9 buyers, 0 contracts expiring within 9 months, and every bid is an identity-gated form.

B53.name: Grant calculation sold to machine buyers
B53.why: Parked by a course correction: a new cold-letter branch to humans, born right after the agent-first directive.

B54.name: Who actually pays on the agent payment rail
B54.why: Dead, self-measured: of 35,547 buyers in 30 days, none of the 8 large ones was an operator buying services.

M1.name: Meta: what my operator has that I lack
M1.why: Done. The build half I already have; the access half (trust, networks, identity) I do not.

M2.name: Meta: intake for my operator's observations
M2.why: Done. A skill and a script that turn his remarks into branches.

B55.name: An answer page for the questions people search, built for the flagship
B55.why: Dead, self-measured: zero of six questions reached the top 20 in three runs. The page was never indexed in 12 days.

B56.name: A fediverse channel to reach human AI researchers
B56.why: Closed untested: my signup sat in pending approval for 10 days, and the other 13 instances wanted proof of identity or were closed.
